svg.aria-label: Blueprint sheet of the codevira internal architecture: six bands from process entry down to disk, drawn as runtime call edges, with the three layer boundaries that leak marked L1 to L3.
svg.title: Codevira internals — blueprint sheet: modules, layers, and which boundaries actually hold
svg.desc: A contributor-facing drafting sheet of the Python packages, drawn dark so it stays legible on both GitHub themes. Six bands: (A) process entry — server.py for MCP stdio, cli.py, the opt-in http_server.py, and three external hook entry points under engine/wiring; (B) the 48 flat files in mcp_server root, grouped by role rather than package — CLI subcommands, install and IDE registration, bootstrap and self-heal, and server-side features; (C) tools/ and engine/ drawn as siblings rather than a stack, because tools/ never imports engine/ while engine/ imports tools/ at three sites, and server.py calls pre_call and post_call around the dispatch; (D) two separate persistence stacks — decisions go through storage/ record stores into jsonl_store.py and atomic.py, while the code graph goes through indexer.sqlite_graph with no storage wrapper at all; (E) two on-disk directories with different lifecycles, .codevira/ canonical and team-shared including graph/graph.db, and .codevira-cache/ per-machine and rebuildable; (F) cross-cutting infra led by paths.py, which 44 distinct modules import. The organising fact is that 479 of 586 internal imports are function-local, so the real structure is a graph of runtime call edges, not module-scope import edges. Three boundary leaks are called out: engine to tools, indexer to and from mcp_server, and storage to indexer. A drafting title block at the foot of the sheet carries the project name, drawing title, sheet number and revision 4.0.1.
svg.text: Codevira internals — modules, layers, and which boundaries actually hold
479 of 586 internal imports (82%) sit inside function bodies; 69 of 127 modules have no module-scope internal import at all.
A static import graph would draw this codebase as disconnected leaves. Every arrow below is a RUNTIME call edge, not an import edge.
every process starts in exactly one of these four
48 flat .py files, ~21.5k loc — there are no subpackages here, so group them by role
R1 entry/transports (4 files, ~6.2k) is band A · R6 cross-cutting infra (10 files, ~2.6k) is band F — the six roles partition all 48 exactly, no orphans.
Sibling placement is inferred from server.py calling pre_call / post_call AROUND the dispatch — the import graph alone does not settle it.
server.py call_tool() — one funnel for all 37 tools, fixed order:
bind client roots → opt-in gate → auto_init → register_default_policies() → pre_call → 38-arm if/elif → post_call → one json.dumps
Every pre-dispatch step is wrapped in `except Exception: pass` — the engine can never block dispatch by failing.
a single “storage” box would be the tidy lie
The decisions half is layered. The code-graph half has no storage wrapper at all — tools/ imports SQLiteGraph from indexer/ directly.
its only internal import is storage/atomic.py
19 files bypass jsonl_store and call it directly — see note 2
NO storage-layer wrapper on this side
tools/{graph, search, learning} import SQLiteGraph at module scope
two directories, different lifecycles — .codevira/ is meant to be committed; this repo gitignores its own (dogfood)
reached from every band above — drawn last because it belongs to none of them
44 distinct modules import it, 5 of them in indexer/.
storage/paths.py is a second, thinner module that delegates here.
a clean layer stack would be a lie — these three edges are the ones to know before you refactor
engine/ → tools/ · 3 sites (signals.py ×2, policies/post_edit_refresh.py) — the only edge that inverts the sibling relation.
signals.impact() swallows all exceptions → {} → BlastRadiusVeto returns allow. A shape change in tools.graph.get_impact silently DISABLES the veto.
indexer/ ↔ mcp_server/ · both directions — 29 statements down across 17 files, 24 up across 6 files.
16 of the 24 upward sit in index_codebase.py. indexer/ is not a lower layer you can read in isolation.
storage/ never imports tools/ or engine/ (0 hits), so it is close to a sealed bottom layer — but it is not sealed.
1 · Arrows are runtime call edges. Because 82% of internal imports are function-local, a module-scope import graph would show almost none of this structure.
2 · Two choke points, not one: jsonl_store.py is the append-only-record choke point, atomic.py the universal file-write one. 19 files bypass jsonl_store and
call atomic_write_text() directly — including tools/roadmap.py and tools/skills.py (a two-layer skip) and indexer/graph_generator.py (outside mcp_server).
3 · mcp_server/__init__.py imports cli at module scope, so reading __version__ pulls in cli.py + indexer — 4 internal modules, 0.04 s. That is a cost, not a
cycle: a Tarjan run over the module-scope graph finds no multi-module SCC larger than 2. A _version.py leaf would remove it.
4 · Registry: 37 Tool() literals against 38 dispatch arms. The extra arm is the search_codebase tombstone, removed in v2.2. 36 tools are advertised by
Measured from source at HEAD 9e53a4e over 127 .py files / ~47k loc. LOC are rounded on purpose — they move every commit. File counts, the import ratio
and the boundary facts are the stable part; re-run the greps in note 2 and panel L1–L3 if you want to falsify anything here.
Local-first MCP server. Runtime call edges across bands A–F; boundary leaks flagged L1–L3.
